Cross-repo change for core work item CG-0MUNC7FK5001T5CP (F7: Main Street first consumer).

Adds src/MainStreetAchievements.ts mapping every CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES id to persistent achievements via the engine-generic @core-engine/AchievementSystem, wired into the challenge completion callback in MainStreetChallenges.ts. No Steam SDK code in this repo; the sink resolves to the renderer IPC client in the Electron launcher and to a no-op elsewhere.

Updates the core submodule to a commit containing the achievement layer (F3) and renderer client (F6). Adds tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts (mapping completeness, launcher-manifest drift guard, idempotent unlock, sink delegation, completion-path wiring).

Core parent: CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `MainStreetAchievements.ts` declares an achievement manifest mapping every `CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES` id to an achievement id with a title, description, and hidden flag; an automated test asserts every template is mapped exactly once.
- [ ] Challenge completion (including the mid-turn `evaluateChallengesAfterAction` path) unlocks the mapped achievement through the engine `AchievementSystem` exactly once per run, with no Steam SDK import anywhere in this repo.
- [ ] In the Electron launcher the unlock is forwarded over the F6 renderer client; in the browser and headless builds it uses the no-op or local sink and the game stays fully playable.
- [ ] Unit tests in the game repo cover mapping completeness, idempotent unlock, and sink delegation; they pass under `--project unit`.
- [ ] The mapping is validated against the launcher manifest (F4) so drift fails an automated check; the cross-repo change is committed and pushed to the game repo's `dev` branch only.

# Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)

## Goal

As a distribution operator, I want a signed pack catalogue hosted at a
configured URL to be discovered at runtime and merged into the player's card
pool, so that I can publish packs without rebuilding the game; as a player I
want those packs to show up in my Card Packs panel exactly like bundled packs.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 1 and 6; parent scope items 1, 2, 6;
parent constraints "reuse existing seams", "totality", "additive", "signing key
separation"; locked decisions Q1 and Q2).

## Context

This is the tracer bullet: it cuts every layer once, end-to-end, so the whole
seam is proven before it is hardened. `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` already provides
`PackSource` / `PackSourceRegistry` and adapts a registry to the loader's
`fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` / `fetchAsset` seams, so **no core loader change**
is needed. The remote source is a provider on that registry.

Without this slice there is no usable increment: a signature gate is
inseparable from discovery (an unverified catalogue must never contribute
packs), so verification lands with the first end-to-end path rather than as a
separate layer.

## Scope

1. **Configuration surface.** Read the remote catalogue coordinates from
   `import.meta.env` (`VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL`,
   `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_PUBLIC_KEY`), validate them, and derive the host
   allow-list. Inert when unset.
2. **Allow-listed bounded fetch primitive.** One total text-fetch helper: refuse
   a host that is not configured (before any request), enforce a hard timeout
   via `AbortController`, map every failure to `null` + one warning.
3. **Signed-manifest verification.** The signed envelope, its deterministic
   canonical payload bytes, pinned-key import from raw base64, and a total
   verifier returning a discriminated result (never throws).
4. **Remote pack source.** `createRemotePackSource(config)` serving
   `<base>/packs/manifest.json` and `<base>/packs/<gameId>/<packId>/cards.csv`
   after verification, rejecting the **whole source** on any verification or
   manifest-shape failure.
5. **Composition and boot wiring.** Compose the registry as bundled source
   first, then the remote source; use it on the browser boot path
   (`bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks`) without touching the Electron
   content-directory path.

## Design notes

- Ed25519 is available natively in Node 22 WebCrypto and the Playwright
  Chromium used by the browser project — **no new runtime dependency**.
- Verification is memoised per source instance: one manifest fetch and one
  verification per boot, not one per CSV.
- The source's remit is "fetch and refuse only". Merging, precedence and
  duplicate-id rejection stay with the registry and the core merge, which is
  what makes bundled/remote parity automatic.
- Every failure is a warning on the existing logger seam; no UI change
  (decision Q3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Remote discovery.** A pack catalogue hosted at a configured (build-time)
- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Signed-manifest integrity.** A remote manifest whose Ed25519 signature is
- [ ] `src/MainStreetRemotePackConfig.ts` parses and validates `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL` and `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_PUBLIC_KEY` (injectable env for tests) and exposes an allow-list predicate; unset, blank or invalid configuration yields no remote sources and logs a warning rather than throwing.
- [ ] `src/MainStreetRemotePackManifest.ts` exports the signed envelope type and a deterministic canonical-payload function, plus `verifyPackManifestSignature(...)` returning `ok` / `missing-signature` / `invalid-signature` / `malformed-envelope` / `unavailable` and never throwing for any input.
- [ ] A manifest signed with the matching private key verifies `ok`; a one-byte body change or a signature from a different keypair returns `invalid-signature`; a blank or absent signature returns `missing-signature`; a non-JSON or wrong-shape envelope returns `malformed-envelope`.
- [ ] The canonical payload is stable under input key reordering so an external operator can reproduce the signed bytes; asserted by a test.
- [ ] A total fetched-text helper refuses a non-configured host **without calling the injected `fetch`**, and maps timeout, rejection, non-2xx and body-read failure to `null` with one warning.
- [ ] A `createRemotePackSource(config)` factory returns a `PackSource` whose `id` distinguishes it from the bundled source, serving `manifest.json` and `<gameId>/<packId>/cards.csv` from the configured base once the manifest verifies.
- [ ] A remote pack served by a fake transport appears in `loadMainStreetCardPacks` merged pool with its cards and reaches the Card Packs listing input; asserted by a test.
- [ ] A missing, invalid, non-pinned-key or malformed manifest makes **every** path from that source resolve `null`, logs exactly one source-level warning, and never throws.
- [ ] The remote source never throws for any input (invalid config, non-string path, empty path, throwing transport), asserted by a table-driven test.
- [ ] `bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks` composes the configured remote source on the browser path, while an explicit launcher `contentDir` composes no remote source and performs no remote fetch (asserted with a spy).
- [ ] No new entry is added to `package.json` dependencies.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetRemotePackConfig.ts` (new)
- `src/MainStreetRemotePackManifest.ts` (new)
- `src/MainStreetRemotePackFetch.ts` (new)
- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts` — `createRemotePackSource`, composition
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — boot wiring on the browser path
- `./env.d.ts` — declared env vars
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackDiscovery.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackIntegrity.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/fixtures/remotePackFixtures.ts`

## Deliverables

- The end-to-end discovery path: configured URL → verified manifest → served
  CSV → merged pool → listing.
- The configuration, verifier and fetch primitives the later slices harden.
- Signed-manifest fixtures (keypair generation, signing, tampering, fake
  transport) reused by the verification items.

## Dependencies

None — this is the first slice.
data.title: Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)

# Verify AC1: the finish gate commits the composition it tested

Parent: **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6** — verification of **AC1**. Verification-only: no framework code is edited from this repo (repository boundary, Q1=A).

**Blocked by (SorraAgents):** `SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2` — *Finish gate: test the tree the commit produces, and prove every verdict's provenance* (in progress; the fix for the build-originated `core` gitlink + `configs/engine-pin.json` churn). **Unblock condition:** that item's fixture test and verdict-provenance change are in `dev` (or `in_review`) and recorded on it.

## Goal

As an implement agent, I need proof that a finish on a source-unchanged item commits exactly the engine composition it tested, so a documentation- or evidence-only item can never silently carry an engine bump (and never fails on another engine's suite).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The SorraAgents git-fixture proof is located and cited here by path and test name: a fixture whose submodule checkout `HEAD` differs from the recorded gitlink shows the build-originated pin/gitlink advance is **not** part of the item's commit when the item did not change engine composition.
- [ ] Live proof on **this repo**: from a worktree created at a commit whose `configs/engine-pin.json` lags the engine `dev` tip, `implement.py finish` on a source-unchanged item produces a commit whose `configs/engine-pin.json` and `core` gitlink equal the pre-commit `HEAD` values (no `engine:sync` churn in the commit).
- [ ] The gate verdict JSON for that run is pasted on this item and records the **composed engine SHA** plus the cache provenance (suite ran vs cache-served).
- [ ] Cache-key behaviour is unchanged and confirmed by reading the SA diff (commit hash recorded here): `compute_git_state` remains keyed on `HEAD` + dirty-path content; a green entry recorded against a different engine is never served (`SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L` remains the guard).
- [ ] No pin-policy regression: a normal (non-finish) `npm run build` still runs `engine:sync` and leaves `configs/engine-pin.json` + the `core` gitlink coherent, and the release path still uses `engine:verify` (`tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` green).
- [ ] Evidence recorded: log paths, verdict JSON and commit hashes on this item; any deviation raised as a new work item rather than worked around here.

## Constraints

- No `.pi/` or framework edits; no changes to `core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs` (canonical in Tableau-Card-Engine, remedy C rejected).
- Runs go through the test skill / the finish gate, never ad-hoc suites.
- If the only workable fix turns out to be verify-only `engine:sync`, stop and raise it for producer sign-off (remedy C was rejected).

## Key Files

- `configs/engine-pin.json`, `core` gitlink, `package.json` (`build` runs `engine:sync` first)
- `tests/tooling/engine-checkout-precheck.ts`, `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` — existing guards to reuse for the lagging-pin condition
- SorraAgents: `implement/scripts/implement.py` (`phase_finish`, `git_commit`), `test_cache.py` (`compute_git_state`)

## Deliverables

- Fixture + live evidence and verdict JSON recorded on this item; AC1 marked satisfied on the parent (or a precise gap raised as a new blocked item).

# Verify AC2: changed-scope selection works for this repo

Parent: **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6** — verification of **AC2**. Verification-only: the fix itself lands in SorraAgents (repository boundary, Q1=A).

**Blocked by (SorraAgents):** `SA-0MVL7YOMJ006UMDO` — *test skill: changed-scope mapper does not map vitest `.test.ts` files* — extended on 2026-10-29 with the `suiteCommands` + `groups` requirement and six acceptance criteria for exactly this verification. **Unblock condition:** that item's selector changes (vitest/TS mapping, `suiteCommands` no longer disabling selection, `groups` honoured, named fallback reasons) are in `dev` (or `in_review`) and recorded on it.

## Goal

As an implement agent finishing a work item in this repo, I need a change set covered by a declared `groups` entry (or by a changed vitest test file) to run a targeted selection, so I stop paying the 47-minute full suite for documentation- or evidence-only items.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A change set matching a declared `groups` entry's `paths` (e.g. `hand-bottom-anchor-browser`) produces `scope: changed` with the group's commands in `implement.py finish` (or `run_tests.py --scope changed`) — the `suiteCommands` early-return no longer fires.
- [ ] A change set consisting of a changed/new vitest `*.test.ts` file selects those files (no full-suite fallback).
- [ ] `suiteCommands` still defines only the **full** suite: a run whose change set cannot be safely narrowed still runs the full 3-command suite and reports `scope: full`, so a partial run can never be presented as full-suite evidence.
- [ ] When no subset applies, the fallback names the **specific** reason ("no changed source/test files", "no matching group") instead of the current generic list of causes.
- [ ] Live evidence recorded on this item: a finish log showing `scope: changed` with the selected commands, plus the SHA of the commit that made it possible in SorraAgents.
- [ ] The SorraAgents selector unit tests for this behaviour are cited by path; the local full-suite gate remains unchanged for non-narrowable change sets.

## Constraints

- No `.pi/test-config.json` `groups` additions to work around a broken selector: this item witnesses the framework fix. (If a group is genuinely missing for a recurring area, raise a separate item.)
- No framework edits from this repo; evidence and verification only.

## Key Files

- `.pi/test-config.json` — the 10 declared `groups` and the 3 `suiteCommands` (read-only here)
- SorraAgents: `test/scripts/run_tests.py` (`changed_scope_commands`, `map_changed_to_tests`, `select_group_from_changed_files`), `implement/scripts/implement.py` (`run_tests`, `_run_resolved_suite`)

## Deliverables

- Live `scope: changed` evidence (+ the `scope: full` fallback evidence) recorded on this item; AC2 marked satisfied on the parent or a precise gap raised.

discovered-from: MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O

## Problem

While finishing MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O the dev push ran **no** git hook:

- `git config --get core.hooksPath` → unset
- `.git/hooks/pre-push` → absent (only `post-checkout`, `post-merge`, `post-rewrite` plus `.sample` files)
- the repo's `.githooks/pre-push` exists but is never invoked from this checkout.

Consequences (the documented dev-push integration gates are inert here):

1. **No full-suite gate on dev pushes** — the framework documents the pre-push hook as the deterministic full-suite integration gate (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81); here a red tree can be pushed straight to `dev`. Note this repo's `.githooks/pre-push` in fact only enforces branch policy + context budget + worklog sync — it has no test-suite step at all — so even when wired it would not provide the documented gate.
2. **No protected-branch check** — a regular agent could push to `main`/`master` without the hook's refusal.
3. **No worklog auto-sync on push**.

## Why it matters

Agent push discipline (push only to `dev`, green suite before push, worklog sync) is currently enforced only by agent behaviour, not by the repository. Any audit that assumes "the hook ran the full suite" is relying on something that did not happen.

## Investigation starting points

- How hooks are installed (framework install script and `.githooks/` → `.git/hooks/` wiring) and why `pre-push` is missing here while `post-*` hooks are present.
- Whether `core.hooksPath` should be `.githooks` per clone (and re-set after a fresh clone/worktree).
- Whether `.githooks/pre-push` should gain the `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env` step the framework docs describe.

## Out of scope

Fixing anything about MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O — that item is complete and its evidence came from an explicit `/skill:test` full-scope run.
data.title: Git hooks are inactive on the tce-main-street checkout, so the documented dev-push gates never run
